questions.subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
questions.microTopic: Inclusive growth and issues arising from it
questions.questionText: Explain the concept of ‘inclusive growth’ and outline the key measures taken by the government towards  achieving it.

answers.answerText:
| **Approach:** • Introduce your answer by defining inclusive growth.
• In the body, first explain the concept by listing its key attributes.
• Next, outline the key measures taken by the government towards achieving it.
• Conclude the answer by highlighting the significance of inclusive growth in Amrit Kaal. | | --- | **UNDP defines** inclusive growth as the **process and the outcome** where all groups of people have **participated in** **growth and have benefited** equitably from it. Following are the key characteristics of inclusive growth: **1.** a) **Broad-based growth** that is spatially distributed (rural-urban) and sectorally diversified (primary, secondary, tertiary sectors); b) pro-poor orientation** addressing income disparities through productive employment generation.** **2.** a) **Equality of opportunity** across social divides (gender, caste, religion); b) participatory development** involving beneficiaries in economic **planning and implementation**;** c) systemic resilience** building and **inter-generational** sustainability (climate resilience, disaster preparedness).** The government has taken several **measures towards achieving it.** They are discussed below: 1. a) **Enhanced participation** of marginalized communities in governance through **mandatory** **representation** (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) and **reserved executive positions** (SC/ST Sarpanch reservations); b) **institutional mechanisms** for equitable access (TRIFED, Stand Up India) facilitating **long-** **term empowerment**; c) affirmative action** in public employment (4% reservation for persons with disabilities).** 2. a) Food and nutrition security** through targeted interventions (NFSA, POSHAN Abhiyan);** b) **human** **capital development** via **educational advancement** (RTE 2009, SSA), **healthcare strengthening** (AB- PMJAY, NMHP), and **skill enhancement** (PMKVY); c) **employment generation** through **productive** **opportunities** (ELI) and **entrepreneurship support** (MUDRA, Start Up India). 3. a) Economic empowerment** through **financial inclusion** (Jan Dhan Yojana), **enhanced credit access** (SHG-BLP, KCC), and **social security expansion** (APY);** b) Infrastructure development** for **balanced** **regional growth** (PMGSY) and **accelerated economic expansion** (capex allocation of Rs. 11.21 lakh crore for FY26);** c) redistributive policies** addressing **income inequality** (progressive taxation) and establishing **income parity** (abolition of privy purse, Kisan Samman Nidhi).** 4. a) Digital inclusion initiatives** (Digital India mission, BharatNet, Common Service Centres);** b) robust** **DPI** ensuring universal access to digital services (UPI ecosystem);** c) cross-sectoral growth promotion** (RKVY, Make in India);** d) quality of life enhancement** (JJM, PMAY);** e) sustainable development** promoting **inter-generational equity** (renewable energy transition, Net Zero by 2070).** **The vision of Viksit Bharat, in Amrit Kaal** would remain unrealized without ensuring **inclusive growth.** Thus, it becomes imperative to prioritize **Sabka Sath Sabka Vikas Sabka Prayas** to fulfill the constitutional mandate of creating a **welfare state.** **(341 words)** **Additional Reading:** **What is Inclusive Growth |ForumIAS** **A Lesson from IIT | Envisioning frameworks for inclusive growth of India through ‘techno-social’ entrepreneurship informed by UN** **SDGs | Education News - The Indian Express** **TRIFED:** Tribal Co-operative Marketing Development Federation of India; **NFSA:** National Food Security Act; **POSHAN:** Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment; **RTE Act:** Right to Education Act; **SSA:** Sarva Shisha Abhiyan; **AB-PMJAY:** Ayushman Bharat- Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana; **NMHP:** National Mental Health Programme; **PMKVY:** Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana; **ELI:** Employment-Linked Incentive**; MUDRA:** Micro Units Development and Refinancing Agency; **SHG-BLP:** Self Help Group- Bank Linkage Programme; **KCC:** Kisan Credit Card; **APY:** Atal Pension Yojana; **PMGSY:** Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana; **DPI:** Digital Public Infrastructure**; UPI:** Unified Payment Interface; **RKVY:** Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana; **JJM:** Jal Jeevan Mission**; PMAY:** Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana

questions.microtag: Distinguish, Explain, Capital Budget, Revenue Budget
questions.questionText: Distinguish between Capital Budget and Revenue Budget. Explain the components of both these Budgets.

answers.answerText:
| **Approach:** • Introduce the answer by giving a brief background of the budget exercise in India and its parts.
• In the body, first distinguish between capital and revenue budget.
• Next, explain the components of both these budgets.
• Conclude by underlining the significance of this distinction. | | --- | **Article 112** of the Constitution mandates the **President** to lay the Budget (**Annual Financial Statement**) of the Union Government **before Parliament**, for every financial year. It comprises **capital budget** and **revenue budget**. The table below discusses the **differences** between them: **Capital Budget** **Revenue Budget** 1. a) Statement of estimated **capital receipts** and 1. a) Statement of estimated **revenues receipts** and **capital expenditure**; b) deals with **investment, asset** **revenue expenditure**; b) deals with **current income** **creation, and liabilities.** **and expenditure** of the government. 2. a) Nature of transactions covered by it is **non-**2. a) Nature of transactions covered by it is **recurring**; **recurring**; b) **high multiplier effect** as the b) **low multiplier effect** as the components under it components under it boosts **employment**, are mainly **consumption-oriented**. **infrastructure**, and economic growth. 3. a) Influence on the **day-to-day functioning of the** 3. a) Influence on broader **development objectives** **government;** b) used to calculate the **revenue** and **economic growth;** b) no such fiscal metric** **deficit (**revenue expenditure-revenue receipts). exists for capital account, although it affects **fiscal** **deficit.**** **Components of capital budget** **1.** **Capital Receipts:** Consist of market borrowings by the government, borrowings from RBI and commercial banks, loans from international organizations, recovery from loans granted by the government etc. **2.** **Capital Expenditure:** Consists spending on acquiring assets (land, buildings, machinery etc), investments in PSUs, investments in infrastructure projects, loans granted by the government etc. **Components of revenue budget** **1.** **Revenue receipts** a) **Tax receipts:** Consist of the proceeds of the taxes and other duties levied by the government. E.g. GST (indirect tax), personal income tax (direct tax), customs duty. **b)** **Non-tax receipts:** Consist of interest receipts, dividends, profits on investment etc. Also includes fees from services rendered by the government and grants-in-aid. **2.** **Revenue expenditure:** a) Consist of expenditure that does not result in creation of assets. E.g. salaries, pensions, interest payments; b) was earlier further classified into **plan** and **non-plan expenditure (**abolished in 2017**).** The **distinction** between capital and revenue budget is a **constitutional mandate** (Article 112 (2)). Simultaneously, it helps provide **clarity on how public monies are being utilised** (whether for immediate operational needs or long-term asset creation), thereby ensuring **transparency in fiscal management. (*****353 words*****)** **Additional Reading** **Union Budget 2025: Understanding Revenue Budget and Capital Budget | Budget 2024 News - Business Standard**
